summary: Specifies how to carry IPv4 datagrams over IEEE 1394 (FireWire) buses, defining the methods, data structures and codes needed. It is a standards-track document at the proposed standard level.

eli5.summary: FireWire is a cable for cameras and drives. This explains how to make it carry Internet traffic too.

questions: how to run ipv4 over firewire
how to send ipv4 over firewire
what is the default mtu for ipv4 over 1394
subtitle: How to carry IPv4 datagrams over FireWire (IEEE 1394), including its own ARP and multicast channel protocol.

tldr.problem: IEEE 1394 (Serial Bus) connects consumer electronics and computers, but it has no standard way to carry IPv4 datagrams, find a node's hardware address from its IP address, or manage multicast.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines an encapsulation header with optional link-level fragmentation, a 32-octet address resolution protocol (1394 ARP), a configuration ROM entry that marks a node as IP-capable, and a multicast channel allocation protocol (MCAP).
tldr.outcome: It makes a Serial Bus usable as an IPv4 network. It warns that Serial Bus is an unsecured link layer, and that the protocols may not work correctly across bus bridges.

today: RFC 2734 is a Proposed Standard from December 1999, and the metadata for this RFC lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It builds on RFC 791 for IPv4 and RFC 2119 for requirement keywords.

sections.title: Why IPv4 Needs Rules for 1394
sections.content:
RFC 2734 specifies how to use IEEE Std 1394-1995 (called 1394 or Serial Bus) to transport IPv4 datagrams. Besides packet formats and encapsulation, it defines an address resolution protocol (1394 ARP) and a multicast channel allocation protocol (MCAP). Both are specific to Serial Bus.

The RFC says Serial Bus links nodes over shared media at speeds from 100 to 400 Mbps, and expects it to form the basis of a home or small office network mixing consumer electronics (digital VCRs, televisions, camcorders) with computer devices (mass storage, printers, tapes).

Addressing is 64 bits: ten bits of bus ID (up to 1,023 buses), six bits of node physical ID (up to 63 per bus) and a 48-bit offset. The 16-bit node ID is like a hardware address, but it is variable and can be reassigned whenever nodes are added or removed.

There is no standard method yet to connect separately enumerated Serial Buses. Unless extended by a future standard, these protocols may not operate correctly across bridges.
sections.eli5: FireWire is like a street where houses can move around every time a new neighbour arrives. This RFC says how to deliver Internet mail on that street.

sections.title: What an IP-Capable Node Must Provide
sections.content:
Not every Serial Bus device can handle IP. An IP-capable node SHALL implement configuration ROM in the ISO/IEC 13213:1994 format, including the bus information block and a unit directory defined by this RFC. Its max_rec field SHALL be at least 8, meaning it accepts block writes and asynchronous stream packets with a 512-octet payload, and can send a 512-octet block response.

It SHALL also be isochronous resource manager capable and SHALL support receiving and sending asynchronous streams, as specified by IEEE P1394a.

The unit directory carries a Unit_Spec_ID entry with value 0x00 005E (the registration ID IANA obtained from the IEEE) and a Unit_SW_Version entry with value one, which says the device follows this standard. Textual descriptors are OPTIONAL; nodes SHOULD use the text IANA and IPv4 if they include them.
sections.eli5: To join the Internet club, a device has to carry a badge saying so, and it has to be able to handle at least a medium-sized package.

sections.title: Encapsulation and Fragmentation
sections.content:
Every IP datagram, 1394 ARP message and MCAP message sent in a 1394 block write or stream packet SHALL be placed inside the packet's data payload behind an encapsulation header. The maximum payload depends on speed: for asynchronous packets it is 512 octets at S100, 1024 at S200 and 2048 at S400. The default MTU is 1500 octets.

When a datagram is larger than the payload both sides can handle, it is split into link fragments. The lf field says where a fragment sits: 0 unfragmented, 1 first, 2 last, 3 interior. datagram_size is one less than the IP Total Length, dgl is a datagram label shared by all fragments, and later fragments carry a fragment_offset. The ether_type is 0x0800 for IPv4, 0x0806 for 1394 ARP and 0x8861 for MCAP.

The receiver identifies fragments of one datagram by the sender's source_ID and dgl. If a new fragment overlaps one already collected, the accumulated fragments are discarded and reassembly may restart with the newest one. A Serial Bus reset makes receivers drop partial datagrams and senders drop unsent fragments.

Stream packets use the global asynchronous stream packet (GASP) format, whose specifier ID is 0x00 005E and whose version is one. The GASP header uses up two quadlets, so the usable payload shrinks by eight octets.
sections.eli5: If a parcel is too big for the box, you cut it into numbered pieces and tape the same label on each. The receiver puts them back together, and if the pieces get mixed up it starts over.

sections.title: 1394 ARP
sections.content:
A node needs to learn the 1394 hardware details of a peer from its IP address. 1394 ARP does this with a 32-octet request or response. Requests are sent the same way as broadcast IP datagrams. Responses may be sent that way too, or as block writes to the sender_unicast_FIFO address named in the request.

Key fields: hardware_type is 0x0018, protocol_type is 0x0800, hw_addr_len is 16, IP_addr_len is 4 and opcode is 1 for a request and 2 for a response. The sender also reports its 64-bit node unique ID, its max_rec, its speed code (sspd, the lesser of link speed and PHY speed, from 0 for S100 to 5 for S3200) and the 48-bit offset of its unicast FIFO, which SHALL NOT change except through a power reset.

A receiver ignores a 1394 ARP message unless the top ten bits of the source_ID are 0x3FF or match its own bus ID.
sections.eli5: It is like shouting 'Who owns this phone number?' and the owner answers with how to reach them, how fast they can talk and where to drop messages.

sections.title: Unicast and Broadcast Delivery
sections.content:
A unicast datagram can go in a block write (asynchronous, with a link-level acknowledgement), in an isochronous stream packet (bounded latency but no acknowledgement), or in an asynchronous stream packet. The last is mentioned only for completeness and SHOULD NOT be used for unicast, because it gives neither acknowledgement nor quality of service and uses up a channel number.

The sender must pick a payload size no larger than what the sender, the recipient and all PHYs in between support. It can learn this from the bus manager's SPEED_MAP or from sender_max_rec in a 1394 ARP response. Best-effort unicast goes in block writes to the source_ID and unicast FIFO learned from ARP. If no acknowledgement arrives, it is uncertain whether the target received the data.

Broadcast datagrams use asynchronous stream packets on the channel in the BROADCAST_CHANNEL register. Nodes SHALL NOT send them while the register's valid bit is zero, which a bus reset clears. This blocks 1394 ARP and broadcast IP until the isochronous resource manager allocates a channel.
sections.eli5: Mail to one friend can come with a delivery receipt. Shouting to everyone uses a shared loudspeaker, and you must wait until it is switched on.

sections.title: Multicast and MCAP
sections.content:
By default, best-effort multicast uses asynchronous stream packets on the broadcast channel, and datagrams for 224.0.0.1 and 224.0.0.2 SHALL use it. A group may use another channel if one is allocated and advertised first, using MCAP messages carried on the broadcast channel with ether_type 0x8861. MCAP messages SHALL NOT be fragmented.

An MCAP message has a length, an opcode (0 Advertise, 1 Solicit) and zero or more group address descriptors. Each descriptor has an expiration time, a channel number from 0 to 63, a speed, a bandwidth field that SHALL be zero and the group address. Messages from other buses are ignored.

A would-be sender listens for an advertisement, expected within ten seconds. If none exists it may allocate a channel from the resource manager's CHANNELS_AVAILABLE register, advertise it, and begin sending once 100 ms have passed. The owner re-advertises at least every ten seconds, with an expiration at least 60 seconds ahead. Solicitations are rate-limited to one per ten seconds.

If two sources map one group to different channels, the owner with the largest physical ID wins and the others stop. A channel mapping that expires is advertised with expiration zero for 30 more seconds before the channel is deallocated. A bus reset invalidates all mappings.
sections.eli5: A group chat can use the shared room, or one member can book a private room and announce it on the loudspeaker every few seconds. If two people book rooms for the same group, the one with the highest number keeps theirs.

sections.title: Security and Registry Notes
sections.content:
The RFC says plainly that it uses an unsecured link layer. Serial Bus is vulnerable to denial of service attacks, and devices can eavesdrop on data or present forged identities. Implementers who use Serial Bus for IPv4 SHOULD consider countermeasures in application or other layers.

On the registry side, IANA must manage a new name space called 'CSR Protocol Identifiers'. A 48-bit number identifies the document that specifies a protocol interface: the IANA registration ID 0x00 005E followed by a 24-bit number IANA administers. The values zero and 0xFF FFFF are reserved, and the value one is allocated to this document.
sections.eli5: Anyone plugged into the cable can listen in or pretend to be someone else, so important secrets need their own lock.

fields.name: lf
fields.desc: Link fragment position; zero when unfragmented.

fields.name: ether_type
fields.desc: Kind of datagram that follows, such as 0x0800 for IPv4.

items.label: Unfragmented
items.desc: The whole datagram is in one packet.

items.label: Interior
items.desc: A fragment between first and last.

fields.name: hw_addr_len
fields.desc: Size of the 1394 hardware address in octets.

fields.name: IP_addr_len
fields.desc: Size of an IPv4 address in octets.

fields.name: opcode
fields.desc: One for a request, two for a response.

fields.name: sender_unique_ID
fields.desc: Node unique ID of the sender.

fields.name: sender_max_rec
fields.desc: max_rec from the sender's bus information block.

fields.name: sspd
fields.desc: Lesser of link speed and PHY speed.

fields.name: sender_unicast_FIFO_hi
fields.desc: High part of the FIFO offset.

fields.name: sender_unicast_FIFO_lo
fields.desc: Low part of the FIFO offset.

fields.name: target_IP_address
fields.desc: Address a request asks about; ignored in a response.

messages.label: MCAP Solicit (opcode 1)
messages.note: Asks owners to advertise sooner; at most one per ten seconds.

messages.label: MCAP Advertise (opcode 0)
messages.note: Maps a group address to a channel; expected within ten seconds.
